newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel bonds close higher, more upside seen.
newsitem.headline: Israel bonds close higher, more upside seen.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed higher on Monday, and traders said they expected further gains in response to news of the central bank's decision to keep interest rates unchanged in August.
Indices:
* Government bonds general: +0.14 pct to 110.32
* CPI-linked government bonds: +0.16 pct to 110.38
* Unlinked government bonds: +0.01 pct 109.93
* Dollar-linked government bonds: +0.17 pct to 110.76
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.01 pct to 108.17
Volume including Makams was an average 133 million shekels.
As most had predicted, the Bank of Israel left its key lending rate for August unchanged at 12.7 percent. It slashed its base lending rate in mid-June by 1.2 percentage points.
"No one was expecting a rise in interest rates today and trading was not affected by the rate publication at the end of the day," said Adam Reuter of the Financial Immunities consulting firm.
Ilan Shabat, investment adviser at Israel Discount Bank said he expected bond prices to rise across the board on Tuesday because of the rate decision.

Unlinked bonds traded mixed on Monday with prices unchanged, but the trend was likley to change on Tuesday, he said. "Maybe there will be demand for these bonds tomorrow because the fear of a rate rise is over. But uncertainty in the market about the next CPI (data) is still high," he said.
"Demand for CPI-linked bonds is continuing because of fears of inflation. There are fears that the rise of the dollar against the shekel will affect inflation," Reuter said.
Yields of CPI-linked bonds ranged between 3.85 to 4.00 percent, Reuter said.

Israel's CPI rose by a steep 1.1 percent, in June, and the shekel's sharp fall against the dollar that month triggered fears the rising inflation trend will continue. The shekel has since recovered some of its losses against the dollar.
"Demand is up for CPI-linked bonds because of fears of inflation but also because supply of these bonds is tight. This week there will be no new issues of CPI-linked bonds," said Shabat.
In the coming six months supply of CPI-linked bonds was expected to tighten because redemptions were expected to exceed new issues, Shabat said.
"Prices of dollar-linked bonds rose today on the rise of the dollar against the shekel on Friday," Shabat said.
The shekel firmed against the dollar on Monday. The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.5450 shekels compared with 3.5530 on Friday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
($1 = 3.54 shekels)
